whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a public road agency) is involved. An attorney can spot that issue early and keep your claim on track.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cost You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation gets reduced by your percentage of blame, even if you're mostly not at fault. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to shift blame onto you, so it's worth thinking twice before giving one.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no limit on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. Preserving evidence quickly, photos, medical records, witness contacts, helps support the full value of what you experienced.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Arvin?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government-owned road or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's best to get information sooner rather than later.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and doing so can sometimes be used against you later. Speaking with an independent attorney first can help you understand what to say and what to avoid.

items.question: Why do crashes seem to happen so often on weekend nights in Arvin?
items.answer: Public crash records show Arvin's reported collisions tend to cluster on Saturdays between roughly 8 and 10 p.m., which may reflect higher traffic volume during that window. That pattern doesn't determine fault in any specific case, but it's useful context if your accident happened during that time.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you receive a recovery.
